item.title: Hamstring MET
clinicalUse: Hamstring flexibility limitation without acute tear
stabilization: Pelvis stabilized to avoid posterior tilt substituting for hip flexion.
contact: Support heel/calf and distal thigh as needed.
forceDirection: Move into comfortable straight-leg-raise barrier; patient gently pushes leg downward/into extension against resistance.
mistakes: Treating acute hamstring strain with aggressive MET.
item.visualCue: SLR barrier → Gentle downward isometric → Relax → Slightly more range.

subTechniques.name: Iliopsoas — MET
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve hip-extension tolerance when hip-flexor guarding or shortness is clinically relevant.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Modified Thomas-style position or side-lying with the pelvis stabilized. Move the treated hip gently toward extension until the first comfortable barrier.
subTechniques.contact: Stabilize the pelvis to prevent anterior tilt; support the distal thigh.
subTechniques.direction: Ask the patient to gently flex the hip toward the ceiling against resistance. Relax, then allow a small increase in hip extension without lumbar extension.
subTechniques.dosage: 3–5 contractions of 5–10 seconds at about 10–20% effort.
subTechniques.reassess: Hip extension, walking stride and Thomas-position response.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: The pelvis is the reference point. If it anteriorly tilts, the technique becomes a lumbar-extension movement.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Avoid forcing hip extension in acute anterior hip pain or after surgery without clearance.

subTechniques.name: Hip Adductors — MET
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve painful/restricted hip abduction when adductor tone is clinically relevant.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supine with the opposite leg stable. Abduct the treated hip to the first comfortable barrier while keeping the pelvis level.
subTechniques.contact: Support the distal thigh/leg and stabilize the opposite pelvis.
subTechniques.direction: Ask the patient to gently pull the leg inward into adduction against resistance. Relax, then take up a small amount of additional abduction.
subTechniques.dosage: 3–5 contractions of 5–10 seconds at low effort.
subTechniques.reassess: Hip abduction, adductor-related pain and side-step/squat tolerance.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: Keep the pelvis from rolling toward the treated side; otherwise the apparent gain is pelvic motion.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Avoid aggressive abduction with acute groin injury or adductor tear.

subTechniques.name: Piriformis / Deep External Rotators — MET
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve selected hip internal-rotation/adduction tolerance when posterior hip guarding is relevant.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supine with the hip flexed comfortably. Move gently toward internal rotation/adduction until the first non-painful barrier.
subTechniques.contact: Stabilize the pelvis and control the knee/distal thigh.
subTechniques.direction: Ask the patient to gently push the knee outward toward external rotation/abduction against resistance. Relax, then take up the new comfortable range.
subTechniques.reassess: Hip internal rotation, seated figure-four tolerance and the patient's functional task.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: Posterior hip pain has many possible sources; do not label all of it 'piriformis syndrome.'
subTechniques.safetyNote: Stop if the position reproduces strong distal neural symptoms.
